data.name: Amresh
data.gender_notes: Amresh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Amresh is a Sanskrit name derived from the root words 'amara' (immortal) and 'rish' (sage). It is a name of great reverence and respect, often given to those deemed wise and knowledgeable. In Hindu mythology, the gods are often referred to as 'Amresh' or 'Immortal' due to their eternal nature. The name Amresh carries the meaning “Immortal, Everlasting” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amresh usually hope their child will grow to embody immortal, everlasting and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May one's wisdom and knowledge be everlasting.

This name has been esteemed for centuries and is often given to those who display these qualities. It is believed that those who bear this name will live a long and fulfilling life, and will be revered and respected by their community.

Those who are given this name are encouraged to tap into their inner wisdom and seek knowledge and understanding in all aspects of their life. The name Amresh is a constant reminder of the ultimate goal of life - to transcend the physical form and attain immortality of the soul.

historical_references.reference: Amreshwar, a form of Shiva, is believed to have been mentioned in the 'Shiv Purana'. This text describes the time when the god Rudra (Shiva) was asked by the gods to reduce the intensity of his terrible form and make the universe habitable. Amreshwar is thus considered the giver of immortality and prosperity.

Amresh Mishra, a renowned Odia (Oriya) poet and scholar, was born around 1869 in the village of Kendrapara in the eastern Indian state of Odisha. He is best known for his works 'Gangadhar Meghana' and 'Rasakeli'. These poetic compositions reflect the rich cultural heritage and language of Odisha, and Amresh Mishra is considered a significant figure in the development of modern Odia literature.
